In Toluca Lake, the jump from two bedrooms to three can come with a significant jump in price. At 10207 Camarillo Street, the third bedroom may already be hiding within the existing floor plan. Set on a generous 7,613-square-foot corner lot, this approximately 1,448-square-foot home pairs classic character, abundant natural light, and multiple living spaces with something increasingly hard to find: the opportunity to rethink a home without necessarily having to make it bigger.

Currently configured with two bedrooms and two bathrooms, the floor plan holds an intriguing possibility. The oversized den already includes a full bathroom and is currently accessed from the dining room. By closing off that interior doorway, the space could potentially be reimagined as a large private primary suite, creating the potential for a three-bedroom configuration largely within the home’s existing footprint.

In a market where the jump from two bedrooms to three can come with a significant price increase, this floor plan is worth considering differently.

Large windows bring sunlight throughout the interiors, while the home’s classic architecture gives the next owner a strong foundation to update thoughtfully rather than start from scratch. There is room here to preserve the character, introduce a more modern point of view, and create a home that feels entirely personal. Outside, the corner lot offers another canvas. Mature lemon and orange trees already dot the property, with plenty of room to imagine outdoor dining, gardens, entertaining spaces, or a more private backyard retreat.

And then there is the location. Just moments from Toluca Lake, you are close to Universal Studios, Warner Bros. Studios, Lakeside Golf Club, and the restaurants, coffee shops, and creative energy of the North Hollywood Arts District. It is the kind of location that can make a morning coffee, studio commute, dinner out, or weekend adventure feel remarkably convenient.

Now offered at a significantly improved price, 10207 Camarillo Street presents an increasingly compelling proposition: buy the space that is already here, then decide what you want it to become. A potential three-bedroom home. A generous corner lot. A backyard ready to be reimagined. A home shaped around the way you actually want to live.

The space is already here. The opportunity is in how you use it.

record.remarks: Panoramic ocean views. New 2026 construction. A licensed Airbnb. This professionally designed coastal retreat in Imperial Beach, California checks every box today's buyer is searching for, with a level of craftsmanship and thoughtful detail rarely found on the market. From the moment you arrive, this three-bedroom, four-bathroom residence signals that it was designed by professionals with an eye for unique, one-of-a-kind fixtures throughout — a home built not just to be lived in, but to be experienced. This is not a spec home dressed up for the market; it is a residence where every decision, from the placement of the windows to the selection of a single light fixture, was made deliberately, with the ocean as the ultimate backdrop. Properties that combine true panoramic ocean views with this level of design rarely come to market in Imperial Beach, and even more rarely do they pair that view with the everyday livability, efficiency, and flexibility built into this home. This is a home for buyers who have looked at plenty of ocean-view listings and found most of them asking for compromise — on layout, on finishes, on functionality. This one asks for none. Step through the entry and the scale of the home reveals itself immediately. Soaring high ceilings draw the eye upward, while walls of floor-to-ceiling windows flood every room with natural light from sunrise to sunset. Light and bright ceiling fans throughout keep the airy, sunlit feel going year-round. Rich wood flooring runs throughout the main living areas,SqFT includes Roof topdeck of 650'sqft  **Living in Imperial Beach: The Area & The Lifestyle** Imperial Beach is the southernmost city on the California coast, tucked into San Diego County's South Bay just north of the U.S.–Mexico border and connected to Coronado by the scenic Silver Strand. It's a place still known, first and foremost, for its beach: nearly four miles of wide, sandy coastline anchored by the iconic Imperial Beach Pier, one of the longest wooden piers on the West Coast. Surfers have long prized the area's breaks, including the legendary Tijuana Sloughs, while beach volleyball, body boarding, and simply spending time along the shoreline are part of daily life here.  What sets Imperial Beach apart from many Southern California coastal towns is its authenticity. This is a working beach community with a genuine, laid-back character — long-standing, family-owned restaurants like El Tapatio and Star Dust Donut Shop have anchored the local food scene for more than four decades, while newer spots like Trident Coffee and Sammy's Woodfired Pizza reflect a town in the midst of a thoughtful revival. Locally loved taco shops, a growing crop of independent retailers, and community gathering spaces like Portwood Pier Plaza give the area a distinctly small-town, community-first feel rarely found this close to the ocean in Southern California.  Nature lovers and outdoor enthusiasts have plenty to explore beyond the sand. The Tijuana River National Estuarine Research Reserve borders the city and is one of the most significant coastal wetlands on the Pacific Coast, drawing birdwatchers and nature photographers from across the region. The Bayshore Bikeway offers miles of scenic, protected cycling along the water, connecting Imperial Beach to neighboring Coronado and beyond. For those craving a truly unique coastal experience, Border Field State Park marks the southernmost beach in the continental United States.  Despite its small-town feel, Imperial Beach offers real convenience: it sits roughly fourteen miles south of downtown San Diego and just minutes from Coronado, putting the city's dining, culture, and employment centers well within reach while still coming home to a quieter, ocean-close setting each day. The climate is one of the area's quiet luxuries as well — mild, semi-arid weather with summers in the upper 70s and winters in the 60s, and sunny or mostly sunny skies on the vast majority of days each year.
